/: An open format and a set of rules that turn a folder of Markdown into a wiki, a graph, an agent memory, a skills library, runnable architectures and a shared live board for agents and people, published here as a node of itself.
/404.html: There is no page at this address.
/about/: Who writes AgenticSystemCore, how people and agents read this node, the status of the specification and how to get in touch.
/clusters/: The groupings this node uses to organise its items.
/concepts/: The twelve terms of the specification, each on its own page with the rules that define it.
/legal/: The licence of each kind of artefact, the Content Use Terms in full, the machine-readable signals and the privacy notice.
/ns/: The vocabulary the graph uses: every class and property with its definition, in Turtle, JSON-LD, RDF/XML and N-Triples.
/procedures/: Step-by-step procedures derived from the specification, each step naming the rule or the check that proves it.
/search/: Search every page and every rule of this site. The index is built with the site, and nothing you type leaves your browser.
/specs/: The twelve sections of the specification, the discovery profile and what a conformance claim is.
/specs/00-overview/: What the specification covers, the words it uses, what it means to conform, and how versions change.
/specs/01-bundle/: The directory that holds a node's knowledge: its layout, slugs, encoding, the one configuration file, the optional agent-lane declarations, and how foreign content comes in and goes out.
/specs/02-item/: One Markdown file with a small YAML header: the keys every item has, what each of the six types adds, the body rules, and the rc.3 additions for ports, architectures, attachments and tasks.
/specs/03-links/: The fourteen typed links between items, the inverses the build computes, the integrity checks, and which links the combiner reads.
/specs/04-canonicalization/: Why two builds anywhere give the same bytes: canonical JSON, NFC text, one time format, fixed sort orders and SHA-256.
/specs/05-graph/: How items become a graph with web addresses, the three RDF views, the ontology and its alignment to SKOS, PROV-O and Dublin Core, and the byte-level pins.
/specs/06-surfaces/: Everything a node publishes: the fixed route set, the discovery document, llms.txt, the chunk export, the JSON-LD context, headers and budgets.
/specs/07-composition/: How a selection of items becomes a verdict and a Harness: the five steps in their fixed order, the seven Harness files, skill packs, ports and saved architectures.
/specs/08-governance/: Who made what and who approved it: provenance, sign-off trailers, gates, the four agent-safety lints, the optional agent lane and the ledger derived from git history.
/specs/09-conformance/: How a claim is made and checked: classes and Levels, the vector format, the command-line contract, the error-code registry and the independent validators.
/specs/10-implementation-profiles/: The four Levels of conformance, how an existing wiki or CMS becomes a node, how two nodes check each other, project mode with tasks and boards, and the LiveBoard.
/specs/11-boundary/: Where a node meets the outside: cross-origin access, the nine parts of federation, the plugin contract for every agent surface, visibility, retirement and tombstones.
/specs/agentic-knowledge/: The profile of the discovery document: how a client finds it, what it looks like, the relations and attributes it may carry, and how it relates to other work.
